newsitem.title: UK: Britain bans sales of some fireworks after deaths.
newsitem.headline: Britain bans sales of some fireworks after deaths.

text.p: Britain on Friday banned the public sale of certain powerful fireworks after the deaths last month of two people while trying to light them.
Consumer Affairs Minister John Taylor said he was introducing emergency regulations to prevent further tragedies at Christmas and New Year parties.
The types of fireworks banned, which are generally imported from China, are known as aerial shells and aerial maroons, and have to be launched from mortar tubes.
The two Britons whose death triggered the move were a headmaster and an employee in the financial services industry.
They were killed on November 5, a day Britons mark with firework displays to commemorate a failed 17th century plot to blow up parliament.
Taylor said in a statement that the banned fireworks "pose a very high risk to users which cannot be adequately addressed by publicity or purely voluntary measures".
He said the fireworks would still be available for professional firework display organisers to buy.
